units.zh: 仁自兩漢以來，外戚之家罕有全者，其傾覆之跡，逆亂之機，皆詳諸前史。
units.en: Since the Han dynasties, few consort clans have survived unscathed—their falls and the seeds of rebellion are fully recorded in earlier histories.
units.literal: Since the Two Han dynasties, few households of imperial affines have been preserved intact; the traces of their ruin and the occasions of rebellion and disorder are all set forth in detail in the earlier histories.

units.zh: 齊氏后妃之族，多自保全，唯胡長仁以譖訴貽禍，斛律光以地勢被戮，俱非女謁盛衰之所致也。
units.en: Among Northern Qi empresses’ kin, many kept themselves safe; only Hu Changren fell to denunciation, and Hulu Guang was killed for his territorial power—neither owed simply to the waxing and waning of palace women.
units.literal: Among the clans of Qi consorts and empresses, many preserved themselves; only Hu Changren suffered disaster through slander and accusation, and Hulu Guang was executed because of his territorial power—neither was caused by the rise and fall of women’s influence at court.

units.zh: 今依前代史官，述《外戚》云爾。
units.en: Following earlier historians, I here present the account of Imperial Affines.
units.literal: Now, following the historians of former ages, I set forth the “Imperial Affines” as follows.

units.zh: 趙猛，太安狄那人。
units.en: Zhao Meng was from Di in Tai’an.
units.literal: Zhao Meng was a native of Di in Tai’an.

units.zh: 姊為文穆皇帝繼室，生趙郡王琛。
units.en: His elder sister was Emperor Wenmu’s successor consort and bore Zhao Commandery Prince Chen.
units.literal: His elder sister was the successor consort of Emperor Wenmu and bore Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen.

units.zh: 猛性方直，頗有器幹。
units.en: Meng was upright and capable.
units.literal: Meng was upright by nature and possessed considerable ability.

units.zh: 高祖舉義，遷南營州刺史，卒。
units.en: When Gaozu rose in arms, Meng was made inspector of South Ying Province, where he died in office.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozu raised the righteous standard, Meng was transferred to be Inspector of South Ying Province and died in office.

units.zh: 婁叡，字佛仁，武明皇後兄子也。
units.en: Lou Rui, styled Foren, was a nephew of Empress Wuming.
units.literal: Lou Rui, courtesy name Foren, was a nephew of Empress Wuming.

units.zh: 父壯，魏南部尚書。
units.en: His father Zhuang served Wei as Minister of the Southern Department.
units.literal: His father Zhuang was Minister of the Southern Department in Wei.

units.zh: 叡少好弓馬，有武幹，為高祖帳內都督。
units.en: In youth Rui loved archery and horsemanship, showed martial talent, and served in Gaozu’s personal guard.
units.literal: Rui in youth loved bow and horse, had martial ability, and served as a commander in Gaozu’s personal guard.

units.zh: 從破尒朱於韓陵，累遷開府儀同、驃騎大將軍。
units.en: He fought at Hanling in the defeat of the Erzhu and rose through the ranks to Director of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels and General of Cavalry with Rapid Steeds.
units.literal: He followed in the defeat of the Erzhu at Hanling and was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels and General of Cavalry with Rapid Steeds.

units.zh: 叡無器幹，唯以外戚貴幸，而縱情財色，為時論所鄙。
units.en: Rui had little talent and owed his rank only to kinship with the throne; he squandered himself on wealth and women, and contemporaries held him in contempt.
units.literal: Rui lacked ability and relied solely on his status as an imperial affine for favor; he indulged wealth and women and was despised by contemporary opinion.

units.zh: 皇建初，封東安王。
units.en: At the opening of Huangjian he was made Prince of Dong’an.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Huangjian era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dong’an.

units.zh: 高歸彥反於冀州，詔叡往平之。
units.en: When Gao Guiyan rebelled in Ji Province, Rui was ordered to suppress him.
units.literal: When Gao Guiyan rebelled in Ji Province, an edict ordered Rui to go and pacify him.

units.zh: 還，拜司徒公。
units.en: On his return he was appointed director of the Department of State.
units.literal: On his return he was appointed Director of the Department of State.

units.zh: 周兵寇東關，叡率軍赴援，頻戰有功，擒周將楊檦等。
units.en: When Zhou troops threatened the eastern passes, Rui marched to their relief, won repeated victories, and captured the Zhou general Yang Biao and others.
units.literal: When Zhou forces raided the eastern passes, Rui led troops to relieve them, fought repeatedly with merit, and captured the Zhou general Yang Biao and others.

units.zh: 進大司馬，出總偏師，赴懸瓠。
units.en: Promoted to grand marshal, he took a detached command at Xuanhu.
units.literal: He was advanced to Grand Marshal and went out to command a detached force at Xuanhu.

units.zh: 叡在豫境，留停百餘日，侵削官私，專行非法，坐免官。
units.en: Rui lingered in Yu more than a hundred days, plundering public and private goods and acting with impunity, until he was dismissed.
units.literal: Rui remained in the Yu region more than a hundred days, encroaching on public and private property and acting lawlessly on his own authority; for this he was removed from office.

units.zh: 尋授太尉。
units.en: He was soon appointed grand commandant.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 薨。
units.en: He died in office.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 尒朱文暢，榮第四子也。
units.en: Erzhu Wenchang was Erzhu Rong’s fourth son.
units.literal: Erzhu Wenchang was the fourth son of Rong.

units.zh: 初封昌樂王。
units.en: He was first enfeoffed prince of Changle.
units.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.

units.zh: 其姊魏孝莊皇後，及四胡敗滅，高祖納之，待其家甚厚，文暢由是拜肆州刺史。
units.en: His sister had been Empress Xiaozhuang of Wei; after the Erzhu were overthrown, Gaozu married her and treated her kin lavishly, and Wenchang became inspector of Si Province.
units.literal: His elder sister was Empress of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei; after the four Erzhu were destroyed, Gaozu took her in marriage and treated her family very generously, and Wenchang was therefore appointed Inspector of Si Province.

units.zh: 家富於財，招致賓客，既籍門地，窮極豪侈，與丞相司馬任胄、主簿李世林、都督鄭仲禮、房子遠等深相愛狎，外示杯酒之交，而潛謀逆亂。
units.en: Rich and hospitable, he leaned on his birth to live in extreme splendor. With Ren Zhou, Li Shilin, Zheng Zhongli, and Fang Ziyuan he feigned convivial friendship while secretly plotting revolt.
units.literal: His household was rich in wealth and he gathered guests; relying on his lineage, he pursued luxury to the utmost. With the chief minister’s aide Ren Zhou, registrar Li Shilin, commander Zheng Zhongli, and Fang Ziyuan he was deeply intimate—outwardly they showed the friendship of wine cups, yet secretly they plotted rebellion.

units.zh: 自魏氏舊俗，以正月十五日夜為打竹簇之戲，有能中者，即時賞帛。
units.en: By Wei custom, on the fifteenth night of the first month people played at striking bamboo targets; a hit won silk on the spot.
units.literal: By the old custom of Wei, on the night of the fifteenth day of the first month there was a game of striking bamboo clusters; whoever hit the mark received silk rewards on the spot.

units.zh: 任胄令仲禮藏刀於袴中，因高祖臨觀，謀為竊發，事捷之後，共奉文暢為主。
units.en: Ren Zhou hid a blade in Zhongli’s trousers; when Gaozu came to watch, they meant to strike—and if they succeeded, to set Wenchang on the throne.
units.literal: Ren Zhou had Zhongli hide a knife in his trousers; when Gaozu came to watch, they planned a sudden attack, and if the affair succeeded they would together install Wenchang as ruler.

units.zh: 為任氏家客薛季孝告高祖，問皆具伏。
units.en: Ren’s retainer Xue Jixiao exposed them to Gaozu, and under questioning all confessed.
units.literal: A retainer of the Ren household, Xue Jixiao, informed Gaozu; on interrogation all confessed.

units.zh: 以其姊寵故，止坐文暢一房。
units.en: Thanks to his sister’s favor, only Wenchang’s own household was punished.
units.literal: Because of his sister’s favor, punishment was limited to Wenchang’s household alone.

units.zh: 弟文略，以兄文羅卒無後，襲梁郡王。
units.en: Younger brother Wenlüe inherited the Liang Commandery princedom when Wenluo died heirless.
units.literal: His younger brother Wenlüe, because his elder brother Wenluo died without heirs, inherited the title Prince of Liang Commandery.

units.zh: 以文暢事，當從坐，高祖特加寬貸。
units.en: He should have shared Wenchang’s guilt, but Gaozu spared him.
units.literal: Because of Wenchang’s affair he should have been punished as an associate, but Gaozu specially granted him leniency.

units.zh: 文略聰明儁爽，多所通習。
units.en: Wenlüe was brilliant, quick-witted, and accomplished in many arts.
units.literal: Wenlüe was clever, sharp, and widely accomplished in many arts.

units.zh: 世宗嘗令章永興於馬上彈胡琵琶，奏十餘曲，試使文略寫之，遂得其八。
units.en: Shizong once had Zhang Yongxing play the pipa on horseback through more than ten pieces and asked Wenlüe to write them down; he caught eight.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong once had Zhang Yongxing play the foreign pipa on horseback and perform more than ten pieces; he had Wenlüe transcribe them, and Wenlüe got eight correct.

units.zh: 世宗戲之曰：「聰明人多不老壽，梁郡其慎之。」
units.en: The emperor teased him: “Clever men seldom live long—take care, Prince of Liang.”
units.literal: The emperor jested, “Clever men often do not live long; Prince of Liang, take care.”

units.zh: 文略對曰：「命之修短，皆在明公。」
units.en: Wenlüe answered, “Long life or short is entirely for Your Majesty to decide.”
units.literal: Wenlüe replied, “Whether life is long or short is all in Your Majesty’s hands.”

units.zh: 世宗愴然曰：「此不足慮也。」
units.en: The emperor said, moved, “That is nothing to worry about.”
units.literal: The emperor said sadly, “That is nothing to worry over.”

units.zh: 初，高祖遺令恕文略十死，恃此益橫，多所淩忽。
units.en: Gaozu’s will had granted Wenlüe ten stays of execution; emboldened, he grew ever more insolent.
units.literal: Earlier, Gaozu’s testament had pardoned Wenlüe ten capital offenses; relying on this he grew ever more overbearing and often insulted others.

units.zh: 平秦王有七百里馬，文略敵以好婢，賭而取之。
units.en: Prince Pingqin owned a horse said to run seven hundred li in a day; Wenlüe wagered a fine maid against it and won.
units.literal: The Prince of Pingqin owned a horse worth seven hundred li; Wenlüe matched it against a fine maidservant, gambled, and won it.

units.zh: 明日，平秦致請，文略殺馬及婢，以二銀器盛婢頭馬肉而遺之。
units.en: When Pingqin came to claim his stake, Wenlüe slaughtered horse and maid and sent back their flesh and her head in silver dishes.
units.literal: The next day the Prince of Pingqin came to redeem the stake; Wenlüe killed the horse and the maid and sent him the maid’s head and the horse’s flesh in two silver vessels.

units.zh: 平秦王訴之於文宣，系於京畿獄。
units.en: Pingqin appealed to Wenxuan, and Wenlüe was thrown into the metropolitan prison.
units.literal: The Prince of Pingqin complained to Emperor Wenxuan, and Wenlüe was imprisoned in the capital jail.

units.zh: 文略彈琵琶，吹橫笛，謠詠，倦極便臥唱挽歌。
units.en: In prison he played pipa and flute, sang songs, and when tired would lie down and chant dirges.
units.literal: Wenlüe played pipa and blew the transverse flute, sang ballads, and when weary would lie down and intone dirges.

units.zh: 居數月，奪防者弓矢以射人曰：「不然，天子不憶我。」
units.en: After months in custody he seized his guards’ bow and shot at people, crying, “Otherwise the emperor would never think of me.”
units.literal: After several months he seized his guards’ bow and arrows and shot at people, saying, “Otherwise the Son of Heaven would not remember me.”

units.zh: 有司奏之，伏法。
units.en: Officials reported him, and he was put to death.
units.literal: The authorities reported this, and he was executed.

units.zh: 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為其父作佳傳，收論尒朱榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。
units.en: Wenlüe once paid Wei Shou heavily to glorify his father in print—hence Shou’s likening of Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang.
units.literal: Wenlüe once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold and asked him to write a fine biography of his father; that Wei Shou compared Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang was largely for this reason.

units.zh: 鄭仲禮，滎陽開封人，魏鴻臚嚴庶子也。
units.en: Zheng Zhongli was from Kaifeng in Xingyang, son of Yan, Wei’s director of ceremonial.
units.literal: Zheng Zhongli was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang; he was the son of Yan, Director of Ceremonial of Wei.

units.zh: 少輕險，有膂力，高祖嬖寵其姊，以親戚被昵，擢帳內都督。
units.en: Young and reckless, strong of body, he rose through Gaozu’s fondness for his sister to a post in the personal guard.
units.literal: In youth he was reckless and had physical strength; Gaozu favored his elder sister, and as a kinsman he was treated with intimacy and promoted to commander in the personal guard.

units.zh: 嘗執高祖弓刀，出入隨從。
units.en: He even bore Gaozu’s bow and sword and attended him everywhere.
units.literal: He once carried Gaozu’s bow and blade and attended him in and out.

units.zh: 任胄為好酒不憂公事，高祖責之，胄懼，謀為逆。
units.en: Ren Zhou drank and neglected duty; rebuked by Gaozu, he turned to treason.
units.literal: Ren Zhou loved wine and neglected official business; Gaozu reproved him, and in fear Zhou plotted rebellion.

units.zh: 賴武明婁後為請，故仲禮死，不及其家。
units.en: Empress Wuming Lou pleaded for him, so only Zhongli died and his kin were spared.
units.literal: Thanks to Empress Wuming Lou’s intercession, Zhongli alone was put to death and his family was not implicated.

units.zh: 李祖升，趙國平棘人，顯祖李皇後之長兄。
units.en: Li Zusheng was from Pingji in Zhao and the elder brother of Xianzu’s Empress Li.
units.literal: Li Zusheng was a native of Pingji in Zhao Commandery and the eldest brother of Empress Li of Emperor Xianzu.

units.zh: 父希宗，上黨守。
units.en: His father Xizong had been administrator of Shangdang.
units.literal: His father Xizong was Administrator of Shangdang.

units.zh: 祖升儀容瑰麗，垂手過膝，睦姻好施，文學足以自通。
units.en: Handsome and open-handed, with hands reaching past his knees, he was gracious to kin and literate enough for polite society.
units.literal: Zusheng’s bearing was splendid; his hands hung below his knees. He was kind in kinship and generous in giving, and his literary learning sufficed for ordinary intercourse.

units.zh: 仕至齊州刺史，為徒兵所害。
units.en: He reached the post of Qi inspector before conscript soldiers killed him.
units.literal: He rose to Inspector of Qi Province and was killed by conscript soldiers.

units.zh: 弟祖勳，顯祖受禪，除秘書丞。
units.en: Younger brother Zuxun became palace librarian when Xianzu took the throne.
units.literal: His younger brother Zuxun, when Xianzu received the abdication, was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 及女為濟南王妃，除侍中，封丹陽王。
units.en: When his daughter married the Prince of Jinan, he was made palace attendant and prince of Danyang.
units.literal: When his daughter became consort to the Prince of Jinan, he was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Danyang.

units.zh: 濟南廢，為光州刺史。
units.en: After Jinan’s deposition he was sent to Guang as inspector.
units.literal: After Jinan was deposed, he was made Inspector of Guang Province.

units.zh: 祖勳性貪慢，兼妻崔氏驕豪干政，時論鄙之。
units.en: Greedy and arrogant, with a domineering Cui wife who meddled in affairs, he was widely scorned.
units.literal: Zuxun was greedy and arrogant, and his wife of the Cui clan was overbearing and meddled in government; contemporary opinion despised them.

units.zh: 以數坐贓免官。
units.en: Repeated corruption charges cost him his posts.
units.literal: He was repeatedly dismissed from office for corruption.

units.zh: 無才幹，自少及長，居官皆因內寵，無可稱述，卒。
units.en: Without talent he held office only through court favor; nothing in his career merits praise—he simply died.
units.literal: He had no talent; from youth to old age his offices all came through palace favor, and there is nothing worth recounting—he died.

units.zh: 元蠻，魏太師江陽王繼子，肅宗元皇後之父也。
units.en: Yuan Man was the adopted son of Wei Grand Tutor Prince Jiangyang Ji and father of Suzong’s Empress Yuan.
units.literal: Yuan Man was the adopted son of Yuan Ji, Grand Tutor and Prince of Jiangyang in Wei, and the father of Empress Yuan of Emperor Suzong.

units.zh: 歷光祿卿。
units.en: He rose to director of the imperial household.
units.literal: He served successively as Director of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 天保十年，大誅元氏，肅宗為蠻苦請，因是追原之，賜姓步六孤氏。
units.en: In Tianbao year ten, when the Yuan were massacred, Suzong’s pleas won Man a pardon and the surname Buliugu.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao there was a great slaughter of the Yuan clan; Suzong pleaded bitterly for Man and he was therefore pardoned and granted the surname Buliugu.

units.zh: 尋病卒。
units.en: He soon died of illness.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he died of illness.

units.zh: 胡長仁，字孝隆，安定臨涇人，武成皇後之兄。
units.en: Hu Changren, styled Xiaolong, was from Linjing in Anding and elder brother of Wucheng’s Empress Hu.
units.literal: Hu Changren, courtesy name Xiaolong, was a native of Linjing in Anding and elder brother of Empress Hu of Emperor Wucheng.

units.zh: 父延之，魏中書令。
units.en: His father Yanzhi had been Wei’s secretariat director.
units.literal: His father Yanzhi was Secretariat Director in Wei.

units.zh: 長仁累遷右樸射及尚書令。
units.en: Changren rose to right vice director of the Masters of Writing and director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: Changren was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 世祖崩，預參朝政，封隴東王。
units.en: At Shizu’s death he joined in governing and was made prince of Longdong.
units.literal: When Emperor Shizu died, he took part in deliberating government and was enfeoffed Prince of Longdong.

units.zh: 左丞鄒孝裕、郎中陸仁惠、盧元亮厚相結托。
units.en: Left assistant Zou Xiaoyu and gentlemen Lu Renhui and Lu Yuanliang attached themselves to him.
units.literal: Left Assistant Zou Xiaoyu and Gentlemen of the Palace Lu Renhui and Lu Yuanliang formed a close, trusting bond with him.

units.zh: 長仁每上省，孝裕必方駕而來。
units.en: Whenever Changren entered the provincial offices, Xiaoyu arrived in a matching carriage.
units.literal: Whenever Changren went up to the provincial offices, Xiaoyu would certainly come in parallel carriages.

units.zh: 省務既繁，簿案堆積，令史欲諮都座者日有百數。
units.en: Paperwork overwhelmed the offices; a hundred clerks a day might seek the chief seat.
units.literal: Provincial business was already heavy and documents piled up; clerks wishing to consult the chief seat numbered a hundred or more each day.

units.zh: 孝裕屏人私話，朝退亦相隨，仁惠、元亮又伺間而往，停斷公事，時人號為三佞。
units.en: Xiaoyu drew him aside for private talk and followed him from court; Renhui and Yuanliang slipped in between sessions and stalled the bureaucracy—contemporaries dubbed them the Three Flatterers.
units.literal: Xiaoyu would dismiss others for private talk; after court he would follow along as well, and Renhui and Yuanliang would seize intervals to go too, halting public business—people of the time called them the Three Flatterers.

units.zh: 長仁私遊密席，處處追尋。
units.en: His secret feasts and private parties were notorious.
units.literal: Changren’s private feasts and secret gatherings were pursued and tracked everywhere.

units.zh: 孝裕勸其求進，和士開深疾之，於是奏除孝裕為章武郡守，元亮等皆出。
units.en: Xiaoyu urged him to climb higher; He Shikai, loathing this, had Xiaoyu sent to Zhangwu and the others posted away.
units.literal: Xiaoyu urged him to seek advancement; He Shikai deeply hated this, and therefore memorialized to appoint Xiaoyu as Administrator of Zhangwu Commandery and to send Yuanliang and the others out as well.

units.zh: 孝裕又說長仁曰：「王陽臥疾，士開必來，因而殺之。
units.en: Xiaoyu told Changren, “Feign illness—when Shikai comes, kill him.
units.literal: Xiaoyu again said to Changren, “If the prince feigns illness, Shikai will certainly come, and you can kill him then.

units.zh: 入見太后，不過百日失官，便代其處。」
units.en: See the empress dowager; within a hundred days you lose your post, then you take his.”
units.literal: Go in to see the empress dowager; within no more than a hundred days you will lose office, then take his place.”

units.zh: 士開知謀，徙孝裕為北營州建德郡守。
units.en: Shikai uncovered the plot and sent Xiaoyu to Jiande in North Ying Province.
units.literal: Shikai learned of the plot and transferred Xiaoyu to be Administrator of Jiande Commandery in North Ying Province.

units.zh: 後長仁倚親，驕豪無畏憚。
units.en: Later, secure in his kinship, Changren grew arrogant and fearless.
units.literal: Later Changren, relying on his kinship, was arrogant and feared nothing.

units.zh: 士開出為齊州刺史。
units.en: Shikai left the capital to be inspector of Qi Province.
units.literal: Shikai went out to serve as Inspector of Qi Province.

units.zh: 長仁怨憤，謀令剌士開，事覺，遂賜死。
units.en: Changren, bitter, plotted assassination; discovered, he was ordered to take his own life.
units.literal: Changren, resentful and angry, plotted to have Shikai assassinated; the affair was discovered and he was ordered to die.

units.zh: 尋而後主納長仁女為后，重加贈謚，長仁弟等前後七人並賜王爵，合門貴盛。
units.en: Soon the Later Lord married Changren’s daughter; honors were heaped on the dead, and seven brothers in all were made princes—the clan blazed with rank.
units.literal: Soon afterward the Later Lord took Changren’s daughter as empress and richly added posthumous honors; Changren’s younger brothers and others, seven in all before and after, were granted princely titles, and the whole household flourished in glory.

units.zh: 從祖兄長粲。
units.en: His elder clan cousin was Changcan.
units.literal: His elder clan cousin was Changcan.

units.zh: 父僧敬，即魏孝靜帝之舅，位至司空。
units.en: His father Sengjing was the maternal uncle of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei and rose to Minister of Works.
units.literal: His father Sengjing was the maternal uncle of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei and rose in office to Minister of Works.

units.zh: 長粲少而敏悟，以外戚起家給事中，遷黃門侍郎。
units.en: Changcan was quick and perceptive in youth. As an imperial in-law, he began his career as palace attendant and was transferred to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: Changcan was quick and perceptive in youth; as an imperial in-law he began his career as palace attendant and was transferred to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 後主踐祚，長粲被勑與黃門馮子琮出入禁中，專典敷奏。
units.en: When the Later Sovereign ascended, Changcan was ordered, together with Yellow Gate attendant Feng Zicong, to enter and leave the palace precincts and handle the presentation of memorials.
units.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, Changcan was ordered, together with Yellow Gate attendant Feng Zicong, to enter and leave the forbidden precincts and exclusively manage the presentation of memorials.

units.zh: 世祖崩，與領軍婁定遠、錄尚書趙彥深、和士開、高文遙、領軍綦連猛、高阿那肱、樸射唐邕同知朝政，時人號為八貴。
units.en: When Shizu died, he jointly directed court government with Lou Dingyuan, Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, Gao Wenyao, Qilian Meng, Gao Anagong, and Vice Director Tang Yong. People of the time called them the Eight Nobles.
units.literal: When Shizu died, he, together with army commander Lou Dingyuan, recorder of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, Gao Wenyao, army commander Qilian Meng, Gao Anagong, and vice director Tang Yong, jointly directed court government; people of the time called them the Eight Nobles.

units.zh: 於後定遠、文遙並出，唐邕專典外兵，綦連猛、高阿那肱別總武任，長粲常在左右，兼宣詔令，從幸晉陽。
units.en: Afterward Dingyuan and Wenyao were sent out, Tang Yong managed the external troops, Qilian Meng and Gao Anagong separately oversaw military duties, and Changcan remained constantly at the sovereign's side, proclaiming edicts and following him to Jinyang.
units.literal: Afterward Dingyuan and Wenyao were both sent out, Tang Yong exclusively managed the external troops, Qilian Meng and Gao Anagong separately supervised military responsibilities, and Changcan was constantly at the sovereign's side, also proclaiming edicts and orders, and followed the imperial visit to Jinyang.

units.zh: 後主即位，富於春秋，庶事皆歸委長粲，長粲盡心毗奉，甚得名譽。
units.en: When the Later Sovereign took the throne, he was still young, so all affairs were entrusted to Changcan. Changcan devoted himself to supporting and serving him and gained a strong reputation.
units.literal: When the Later Sovereign took the throne, he was young in years, and all affairs were entrusted to Changcan; Changcan devoted his heart to supporting and serving him and gained a great reputation.

units.zh: 又為侍中。
units.en: He also became palace attendant.
units.literal: He also became palace attendant.

units.zh: 長仁心欲入處機要之地，為執政不許，長仁疑長粲通謀，大以為恨。
units.en: Changren wanted to enter the key councils, but those in power would not permit it. Suspecting that Changcan had conspired against him, Changren deeply resented him.
units.literal: Changren wished in his heart to enter a place of vital importance, but those in power did not permit it; Changren suspected that Changcan had conspired in this and deeply resented him.

units.zh: 遂言於太后，發其陰私，請出為州，後主不得已從焉。
units.en: He then spoke to the empress dowager, exposed Changcan's private misconduct, and asked that he be sent out to a province; the Later Sovereign had no choice but to agree.
units.literal: He then spoke to the empress dowager, exposed Changcan's private misconduct, and requested that he be sent out to a province; the Later Sovereign had no choice but to follow this.

units.zh: 除趙州刺史。
units.en: Changcan was appointed inspector of Zhaozhou.
units.literal: Changcan was appointed inspector of Zhaozhou.

units.zh: 及辭，長粲流涕，後主亦憫默。
units.en: When Changcan took leave, he wept, and the Later Sovereign too fell silent in pity.
units.literal: When he took leave, Changcan shed tears, and the Later Sovereign too was silent with pity.

units.zh: 至州，因沐髮手不得舉，失音，卒。
units.en: After arriving in the province, he was washing his hair when his hand would no longer lift; he lost his voice and died.
units.literal: After arriving in the province, while washing his hair his hand could not be raised; he lost his voice and died.

units.zh: 乙卯，以司徒、平秦王歸彥為太傅，以尚書右僕射、趙郡王叡為尚書令，以太尉尉粲為太保，以尚書令段韶為大司馬，以豐州刺史婁叡為司空，乙太傅、平陽王淹為太宰，以太保、彭城王浟為太師、錄尚書事，以冀州刺史、博陵王濟為太尉，以中書監、任城王潛為尚書左僕射，以幷州刺史斛律光為右僕射，封孝昭皇帝太子百年為樂陵郡王。
units.en: On the yimao day, the emperor reshuffled the highest offices: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, Minister over the Masses, became Grand Tutor; Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, became Chief Minister of the Secretariat; Grand Commandant Wei Can became Grand Guardian; Duan Shao became Grand Marshal; Lou Rui became Minister of Works; Prince Yan of Pingyang became Grand Minister; Prince You of Pengcheng became Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat; Prince Ji of Boling became Grand Commandant; Prince Qian of Rencheng became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Hulu Guang became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Emperor Xiaozhao's crown prince Bainian was made Prince of Leling Commandery.
units.literal: On the yimao day, Minister over the Masses and Prince Guiyan of Pingqin was made Grand Tutor; Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat; Grand Commandant Wei Can was made Grand Guardian; Chief Minister of the Secretariat Duan Shao was made Grand Marshal; Inspector of Feng Province Lou Rui was made Minister of Works; Grand Tutor and Prince Yan of Pingyang was made Grand Minister; Grand Guardian and Prince You of Pengcheng was made Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat; Inspector of Ji Province and Prince Ji of Boling was made Grand Commandant; Director of the Secretariat and Prince Qian of Rencheng was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Inspector of Bing Province Hulu Guang was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Emperor Xiaozhao's crown prince Bainian was enfeoffed as Prince of Leling Commandery.

units.zh: 秋七月，太宰、冀州刺史、平秦王歸彥據州反，詔大司馬段韶、司空婁叡討擒之。
units.en: In the seventh month of autumn, Grand Preceptor, Inspector of Ji Province, and Prince Gao Guiyan of Pingqin seized the province in rebellion. An edict ordered Grand Marshal Duan Shao and Minister of Works Lou Rui to suppress and capture him.
units.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Grand Preceptor, Inspector of Ji Province, and Prince of Pingqin Gao Guiyan seized the province in rebellion; an edict ordered Grand Marshal Duan Shao and Minister of Works Lou Rui to suppress and capture him.

units.zh: 丁酉，以大司馬段韶為太傅，以司空婁叡為司徒，乙太傅、平陽王淹為太宰，以尚書令斛律光為司空，以太子太傅、趙郡王叡為尚書令，中書監、河間王孝琬為尚書左僕射。
units.en: On the dingyou day, Grand Marshal Duan Shao was made Grand Tutor; Minister of Works Lou Rui was made Minister over the Masses; Grand Tutor and Prince Yan of Pingyang was appointed Grand Preceptor; Chief Minister of the Secretariat Hulu Guang was made Minister of Works; Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat; and Director of the Secretariat and Prince Xiaowan of Hejian was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: On the dingyou day, Grand Marshal Duan Shao was appointed Grand Tutor; Minister of Works Lou Rui was made Minister over the Masses; Grand Tutor and Prince of Pingyang Yan was appointed Grand Preceptor; Chief Minister of the Secretariat Hulu Guang was made Minister of Works; Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat; and Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Hejian Xiaowan was made Left Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 壬午，以尚書令、趙郡王叡為錄尚書事，以前司徒婁叡為太尉。
units.en: On the renwu day, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery was appointed recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing, and the former Minister over the Masses Lou Rui was appointed grand commandant.
units.literal: On the renwu day, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery was made recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing, and the former Minister over the Masses Lou Rui was made grand commandant.

units.zh: 甲辰，太尉婁叡大破周軍於軹關，擒楊檦。
units.en: On the jiachen day, Grand Commandant Lou Rui routed the Northern Zhou army at Zhiguan Pass and took Yang Biao prisoner.
units.literal: On the jiachen day, Grand Commandant Lou Rui routed the Northern Zhou army at Zhiguan Pass and captured Yang Biao.

units.zh: 夏四月戊午，大將軍、東安王婁叡坐事免。
units.en: In summer, in the fourth month, on wuwu, Lou Rui, Grand General and Prince of Dong'an, was dismissed over an affair.
units.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the wuwu day, Grand General and Prince Rui of Dong'an, Lou Rui, was dismissed for involvement in a case.

units.zh: 其後，衛青歲以數萬騎出擊匈奴，遂取河南地，築朔方。
units.en: Major anti-Xiongnu campaigns under Wei Qing expanded territory and frontier fortification.
units.literal: Afterward, each year Wei Qing led tens of thousands of cavalry to strike Xiongnu, taking Henan lands and building Shuofang.

units.zh: 此後四年，衛青比歲十餘萬眾擊胡，斬捕首虜之士受賜黃金二十餘萬斤，而漢軍士馬死者十餘萬，兵甲轉漕之費不與焉。
units.en: In the following four years, Wei Qing year after year led more than one hundred thousand troops to strike the Hu. Soldiers who cut off heads and captured enemies received rewards of more than two hundred thousand jin of gold, while more than one hundred thousand Han soldiers and horses died, not counting the costs of armor and transport.
units.literal: In the following four years, each year Wei Qing led over one hundred thousand troops to strike the Hu; soldiers who cut off heads and captured enemies received rewards in gold of over two hundred thousand jin, while over one hundred thousand Han soldiers and horses died—not counting the cost of armor and transport.

units.zh: 廢帝殷，字正道，文宣帝之長子也，母曰李皇后。
units.en: Emperor Fei, whose personal name was Yin and style name Zhengdao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wenxuan. His mother was Empress Li.
units.literal: Emperor Fei, Yin, style name Zhengdao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wenxuan; his mother was Empress Li.

units.zh: 庚戌，尊皇太后爲太皇太后，皇后爲皇太后。
units.en: On the gengxu day he elevated the empress dowager to grand empress dowager and the empress to empress dowager.
units.literal: On the gengxu day he honored the empress dowager as grand empress dowager and the empress as empress dowager.

units.zh: 以晉昌王唐邕為宰輔，齊昌王莫多婁敬顯、沭陽王和阿于子、右纫大將軍段暢、武纫將軍相里僧伽、開府韓骨胡、侯莫陳洛州為爪牙。
units.en: He made Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; Opening-Office General Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou his strong arms.
units.literal: He appointed Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang as chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; General of Opening Gates Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou as his strong arms.

units.zh: 及輿駕在晉陽，武成鎮鄴，望氣者云鄴城有天子氣。
units.en: When the emperor was at Jinyang and Wucheng (Gao Zhan) held Ye, geomancers declared that Ye possessed the aura of imperial destiny.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Jinyang and Wucheng was stationed at Ye, practitioners of qi-reading said Ye city had the aura of a Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 長廣王湛為大司馬、錄幷省尚書事，解京畿大都督。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang was appointed grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration, and was relieved of the capital-region command.
units.literal: Prince Zhan of Changguang was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province, and was relieved as metropolitan commander of the capital region.

units.zh: 戊子，以太傅、長廣王湛為右丞相，以太尉、平陽王淹為太傅，以尚書令、彭城王浟為大司馬。
units.en: On wuzi, Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand tutor, became right chancellor; Prince Yan of Pingyang, then grand commandant, became grand tutor; and Prince You of Pengcheng, director of the Masters of Writing, became grand marshal.
units.literal: On wuzi, the Grand Tutor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was appointed Right Chancellor; the Grand Commandant, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was appointed Grand Tutor; and the Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince You of Pengcheng, was appointed Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
units.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

units.zh: 遣使詔追長廣王入纂大統，手書云：「宜將吾妻子置一好處，勿學前人也。」
units.en: He dispatched envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed him, writing in his own hand: "See that my wife and children are placed somewhere safe; do not do as those before you did."
units.literal: He sent envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed to the great succession, writing in his own hand: "You should place my wife and children in a good place; do not imitate those before you."

units.zh: 帝時以尊親而見猜斥，乃與長廣王期獵，謀之於野。
units.en: Because his rank and kinship made him suspect, Xiaozhao was being pushed aside. He therefore arranged a hunt with Prince Zhan of Changguang and plotted with him in the field.
units.literal: The emperor at that time, because he was an honored kinsman, was regarded with suspicion and pushed aside; he therefore arranged to hunt with the Prince of Changguang and plotted with him in the countryside.

units.zh: 至若負博陸之圖，處藩屏之地，而欲迷邦違難，其可得乎。
units.en: But for one who holds a Huo Guang's map yet stands as a screen for the realm — if he would lose the state and turn from hardship, can he succeed?
units.literal: As for one who bears a Huo Guang's design yet stands in a screen-barricade place — if he wishes to lose the state and defy adversity, can he succeed?

units.zh: 神武明皇后婁氏，諱昭君，贈司徒內干之女也。
units.en: Empress Ming, née Lou, whose personal name was Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Empress Ming, Lady Lou, taboo name Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 神武婁后
units.en: Empress Lou of Shenwu
units.literal: Empress Lou of Shenwu

units.zh: 及拜渤海王妃，閫闈之事悉決焉。
units.en: When she was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.
units.literal: When he was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.

units.zh: 文襄嗣位，進為太妃。
units.en: When Gao Cheng succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.
units.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.

units.zh: 天保初，尊為皇太后，宮曰宣訓。
units.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.

units.zh: 孝昭即位，復為皇太后。
units.en: When Gao Yan succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.
units.literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.

units.zh: 濟南即位，尊為太皇太后。
units.en: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
units.literal: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

units.zh: 太皇太后密與孝昭及諸大將定策誅之，下令廢立。
units.en: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Gao Yan and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing one ruler and enthroning another.
units.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Xiaozhao and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing and enthroning.

units.zh: 大寧二年春，太后寢疾，衣忽自舉，用巫媼言改姓石氏。
units.en: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.
units.literal: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.

units.zh: 孝昭帝崩，太后又下詔立武成帝。
units.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.

units.zh: 及見神武於城上執役，驚曰：「此真吾夫也。」
units.en: When she saw Gao Huan laboring on the city wall, she started and said, "This is truly my husband."
units.literal: When she saw Shenwu performing labor on the city wall, she was startled and said: "This is truly my husband."

units.zh: 乃使婢通意，又數致私財，使以聘己，父母不得已而許焉。
units.en: She sent a maid to convey her feelings and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.
units.literal: She then sent a maid to convey her feelings, and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.

units.zh: 弟昭，以功名自達，其餘親屬，未嘗為請爵位。
units.en: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.
units.literal: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.

units.zh: 太后凡孕六男二女，皆感夢：孕文襄則夢一斷龍；
units.en: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Gao Cheng she dreamed of a severed dragon;
units.literal: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Wenxiang she dreamed of a severed dragon;

units.zh: 孕文宣則夢大龍，首尾屬天地，張口動目，勢狀驚人；
units.en: when she conceived Gao Yang she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;
units.literal: when she conceived Wenxuan she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;

units.zh: 孕孝昭則夢蠕龍於地；
units.en: when she conceived Gao Yan she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;
units.literal: when she conceived Xiaozhao she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;

units.zh: 孕武成則夢龍浴於海；
units.en: when she conceived Gao Zhan she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;
units.literal: when she conceived Wucheng she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;

units.zh: 孕魏二后並夢月入懷；
units.en: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;
units.literal: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;

units.zh: 孕襄城、博陵二王夢鼠入衣下。
units.en: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.
units.literal: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.

units.zh: 四月辛丑，崩於北宮，時年六十二。
units.en: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.
units.literal: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.

units.zh: 五月甲申，合葬義平陵。
units.en: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Gao Huan at Yiping Tomb.
units.literal: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Shenwu at Yiping Tomb.

units.zh: 文宣將受魏禪，后固執不許，帝所以中止。
units.en: When Gao Yang was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.
units.literal: When Wenxuan was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.

units.zh: 神武嘗將西討出師，後夜孿生一男一女，左右以危急，請追告神武。
units.en: Once, as Gao Huan was about to march west on campaign, the empress gave birth at night to twins, a boy and a girl. Those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after him.
units.literal: Once when Shenwu was about to march west on campaign, the empress at night bore twins, a boy and a girl; those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after Shenwu.

units.zh: 后弗聽曰：「王出統大兵，何得以我故輕離軍幕。
units.en: The empress would not hear of it. "The king has gone forth to command a great army," she said. "He cannot lightly leave the command tent on my account.
units.literal: The empress would not listen and said: "The king has gone forth to command a great army — how can he lightly leave the command tent on my account.

units.zh: 死生命也，來復何為！」
units.en: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!"
units.literal: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!"

units.zh: 沙苑敗後，侯景屢言請精騎二萬，必能取之。
units.en: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover the lost ground.
units.literal: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover it.

units.zh: 神武悅，以告于后。
units.en: Gao Huan was pleased and told the empress.
units.literal: Shenwu was pleased and told the empress.

units.zh: 后曰：「若如其言，豈有還理，得獺失景，亦有何利。」
units.en: The empress said, "If things go as he promises, there would be no reason for him to return. You would gain some paltry conquest and lose Hou Jing; there would be no profit in that."
units.literal: The empress said: "If it comes about as he says, could there be any coming back — gain the otter, lose Jing; what profit is there."

units.zh: 乃止。
units.en: Thereupon he desisted.
units.literal: Thereupon he desisted.

units.zh: 及茹茹公主至，后避正室處之。
units.en: When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.
units.literal: When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.

units.zh: 后曰：「國家大計，願不疑也。」
units.en: The empress said, "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate."
units.literal: The empress said: "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate."

units.zh: 性寬厚，不妒忌，神武姬侍，咸加恩待。
units.en: Her nature was generous and free of jealousy; Gao Huan's concubines and attendants she treated with equal favor.
units.literal: Her nature was generous and she was not jealous; Shenwu's concubines and attendants she all treated with favor.

units.zh: 后高明嚴斷，雅遵儉約，往來外舍，侍從不過十人。
units.en: The empress was lofty in judgment, clear-minded, and stern; she always observed thrift, and when she went out to external residences her attendants never exceeded ten.
units.literal: The empress was lofty, clear, and stern in judgment; she always observed thrift; when going out to external residences, her attendants never exceeded ten.

units.zh: 神武既有澄清之志，傾產以結英豪，密謀秘策，后恒參預。
units.en: Once Gao Huan resolved to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems Empress Lou always took part.
units.literal: Once Shenwu had the will to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems the empress always took part.

units.zh: 后未崩，有童謠曰「九龍母死不作孝」。
units.en: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme ran: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."
units.literal: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme said: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."

units.zh: 及后崩，武成不改服，緋袍如故。
units.en: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.
units.literal: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.

units.zh: 論曰：神武肇興齊業，武明追蹤周亂。
units.en: The appraisal says: Shenwu founded Qi's enterprise, but Wuming followed the path of Zhou's disorder.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Shenwu first raised the enterprise of Qi, but Wuming followed the track of Zhou's disorder.

units.zh: 又奉別詔，令共胡長粲輔遵太子，轉庶子。
units.en: By a separate edict he was to assist the crown prince with Hu Changcai and was transferred to heir-apparent subprefect.
units.literal: He was further given a separate edict to assist the crown prince together with Hu Changcai; he was transferred to subprefect of the heir apparent.

units.zh: 先是童謠云：「中興寺內白鳧翁，四方側聽聲雍雍，道人聞之夜打鐘。」
units.en: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell."
units.literal: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell."

units.zh: 道人，濟南王小名。
units.en: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.
units.literal: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.

units.zh: 先是，恒留濟南於鄴，除領軍厙狄伏連為幽州刺史，以斛律豐樂為領軍，以分武成之權。
units.en: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made commander of the army — both to divide Gao Zhan's power.
units.literal: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made Governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made Commander of the Army — both to divide Wucheng's power.

units.zh: 昭帝以為濟南應之，乃使平秦王歸彥之鄴，迎濟南赴幷州。
units.en: Gao Yan thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.
units.literal: Emperor Zhao thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.

units.zh: 武成乃奉詔，令數百騎送濟南於晉陽。
units.en: Gao Zhan thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.
units.literal: Wucheng thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.

units.zh: 鳧翁，謂雄雞，蓋指武成小字步落稽也。
units.en: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Gao Zhan's childhood name Buluoqi.
units.literal: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Wucheng's childhood name Buluoqi.

units.zh: 打鐘，言將被擊也。
units.en: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.
units.literal: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.

units.zh: 因逼之，答曰：「濟南世嫡，主上假太后令而奪之。
units.en: Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.
units.literal: Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.

units.zh: 旣而太史奏言北城有天子氣。
units.en: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.
units.literal: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.

units.zh: 今集文武，示以此勑，執豐樂，斬歸彥，尊濟南，號令天下，以順討逆，此萬世一時也。」
units.en: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity."
units.literal: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity."

units.zh: 初濟南自晉陽之鄴，楊愔宣勑，留從駕五千兵於西中，陰備非常。
units.en: When Prince of Jinan first traveled from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin read the edict leaving five thousand troops of the escort in the Western Quarter — a secret guard against surprise.
units.literal: At first, when the Prince of Jinan went from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin proclaimed the edict and left five thousand troops of the imperial escort in the Western Quarter, secretly preparing against the unexpected.

units.zh: 父高陽王雍，從孝莊於河陰遇害。
units.en: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang to Heyin and met disaster there.
units.literal: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang at Heyin and met disaster there.

units.zh: 元韶，字世胄，魏孝莊之侄。
units.en: Yuan Shao, styled Shizhou, was a nephew of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei.
units.literal: Yuan Shao, styled Shizhou, was a nephew of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei.

units.zh: 莊帝從容謂曰：「王才非荀、蔡，中歲屢遷，當由少長朕家，故有超授。」
units.en: Emperor Zhuang said to him at ease, "Prince, your talent is not like that of Xun or Cai; yet in mid-career you have been repeatedly promoted. That must be because you grew up in my household from youth — hence these extraordinary appointments."
units.literal: Emperor Zhuang said to him at ease: "Prince, your talent is not like Xun or Cai; in your middle years you have been repeatedly transferred — this must be because you grew up young in my household, hence the extraordinary promotions."

units.zh: 莊帝幸洛南，昭業立於閶闔門外叩馬諫，帝避之而過，後勞勉之。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuang visited south Luo, Zhaoye stood outside Changhe Gate, seized the bridle, and remonstrated. The emperor avoided him and rode on, but later commended him.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuang visited the south of Luo, Zhaoye stood outside the Changhe Gate, seized the horse's bridle, and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed by, but later commended and encouraged him.

units.zh: 永安初，復本封咸陽郡王，累遷侍中。
units.en: At the beginning of Yong'an he was restored to his original enfeoffment as prince of Xianyang commandery and rose through repeated promotions to palace attendant.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was restored to his original enfeoffment as Prince of Xianyang commandery; he rose through repeated promotions to palace attendant.

units.zh: 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶
units.en: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao
units.literal: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao

units.zh: 韶逢一老母姓程，哀之，隱於私家十餘日，莊帝訪而獲焉，襲封彭城王。
units.en: Shao met an old woman surnamed Cheng, who pitied him and hid him in her home for more than ten days. Emperor Zhuang searched for him and found him, and Shao inherited the title Prince of Pengcheng.
units.literal: Shao encountered an old woman surnamed Cheng, who pitied him and hid him in her private home for more than ten days; Emperor Zhuang searched for him and found him, and he inherited the title Prince of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 孝昭皇后元氏，開府元蠻女也。
units.en: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao was the daughter of Yuan Man, a Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao was the daughter of Yuan Man, a Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.

units.zh: 宮闈內忽有飛語，帝令檢推，得后父兄書信，元蠻由是坐免官。
units.en: When rumors suddenly circulated inside the palace, the emperor ordered an investigation. Letters from the empress's father and brothers were found, and Yuan Man was dismissed from office for it.
units.literal: Suddenly there was a rumor within the palace; the emperor ordered an investigation and obtained letters from the empress's father and brothers, and Yuan Man was implicated by this and dismissed from office.
